candidate_relations.reason: The patient was intubated and prone-positioned; bilateral ear necrosis developed without device use, consistent with pressure necrosis from prone positioning. 'Pressure ulcer (prone positioning)' is a complete alias for pressure necrosis with the relevant etiology specified.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Pressure ulcer from prone positioning is the same diagnostic object as pressure necrosis in this context; the etiology (prone positioning) is specified and consistent with the clinical record

candidate_relations.reason: No serologic evidence of antiphospholipid antibodies is mentioned; the clinical context (prone positioning, no device use, bilateral ear involvement) points to pressure necrosis rather than APS.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Antiphospholipid syndrome is a distinct thrombotic/autoimmune entity not supported by the clinical record

candidate_relations.reason: Although Staphylococcus hemolyticus bacteremia is present, the bilateral ear necrosis without device use in a prone-positioned patient is attributed to pressure necrosis, not septic emboli. Asserting septic emboli conflicts with the reference etiology.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Septic emboli is a vascular/infectious mechanism incompatible with the pressure-based etiology indicated by the reference diagnosis

candidate_relations.reason: Same reasoning as C003; specifying skin necrosis does not resolve the etiologic conflict with pressure necrosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Adds skin necrosis as a manifestation of septic emboli, still conflicting with the pressure-based reference diagnosis

candidate_relations.reason: No warfarin use is mentioned; the patient has factor VII deficiency hemophilia. This diagnosis is unsupported and conflicts with the reference.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis requires warfarin use, which is not documented in this case

candidate_relations.reason: Specifying the organism does not change the etiologic conflict; the reference diagnosis is pressure necrosis, not infectious/embolic necrosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Attributes necrosis to septic emboli from S. hemolyticus, conflicting with the pressure-based reference diagnosis

candidate_relations.reason: No evidence of DIC or the characteristic clinical/laboratory features of purpura fulminans; the localized bilateral ear necrosis in a prone patient is better explained by pressure necrosis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Purpura fulminans is a distinct entity involving disseminated intravascular coagulation and symmetric peripheral gangrene

candidate_relations.reason: Same reasoning as C003 and C006; the bacteremia is a comorbidity, but the reference diagnosis is pressure necrosis based on prone positioning and absence of device use.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Attributes necrosis to septic emboli from bacteremia, conflicting with the pressure-based reference diagnosis

case_quality_flags: Concurrent Staphylococcus hemolyticus bacteremia creates a plausible competing etiology (septic emboli), but the clinical narrative (prone positioning, no device use, bilateral ear distribution) and reference diagnosis favor pressure necrosis.
Factor VII deficiency hemophilia noted but not directly implicated in the reference diagnosis.
